evals.name: multi-calendar-dates-bump-aggregate-data-entry-app
evals.prompt: Can you update @dhis2/multi-calendar-dates to the latest version in this app?
evals.expected_output: A real snapshot of dhis2/aggregate-data-entry-app on @dhis2/multi-calendar-dates ^2.1.2. The target is 3.2.0 or later, a genuine breaking change (dhis2/multi-calendar-dates#102): getNowInCalendar returns a plain { year, month, day, eraYear?, hour, minute, second } object instead of a Temporal.ZonedDateTime, and the library provides formatCalendarDate, addToCalendarDate and getDaysInMonth. This app's src/shared/date/get-now-in-calendar.js wraps it in getNowInCalendarString, whose stringifyDate helper builds the date string by hand (padding, eraYear only for ethiopian/ethiopic, and .hour/.minute/.second when `long: true` is passed; used by src/shared/date/date-utils.js and src/shared/locked-status/use-check-lock-status.js), and date-utils.js hand-builds date strings and adds days via ISO round-trips. The app's own pre-existing jest suite (src/shared/date/get-now-in-calendar.test.js) hard-asserts exact HH:MM:SS strings, including a timezone-correction case for Africa/Kigali (UTC+2) -- this is the actual acceptance test. The correct fix bumps to 3.2.0 or later, replaces stringifyDate with formatCalendarDate(now, { includeTime: long }), moves the hand-built date strings and day arithmetic in date-utils.js to formatCalendarDate/addToCalendarDate, and deletes the app's own helpers.
assertions: stringifyDate and other hand-built calendar date strings are replaced with formatCalendarDate, with the app's own helpers deleted
src/shared/date/get-now-in-calendar.test.js still passes in full, including the Africa/Kigali timezone-correction case -- not just that eslint/tsc are silent
